newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Election candidate shot dead in Pakistani city.
newsitem.headline: Election candidate shot dead in Pakistani city.

text.p: A politician in opposition leader Benazir Bhutto's Pakistan People's Party (PPP) was shot dead in the Punjab provincial capital of Lahore on Monday, police said.
They said unidentified gunmen, using vehicles decorated with PPP election posters, intercepted Haji Iqbal Ghurki at about one a.m. (1800 GMT Sunday) as he was returning home.

Ghurki, a PPP candidate in a provincial assembly by-election due to have taken place on Monday, leapt from his car and ran down an alley, but his attackers pursued him and shot him with automatic weapons before escaping, police said.

Ghurki, who was in his mid-40s, had served as transport minister in the previous PPP-controlled Punjab provincial government that fell in November after President Farooq Leghari sacked Bhutto on disputed charges of corruption and misrule.
Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif's Pakistan Muslim League (PML) took power after a general election on February 3 and swept to victory in a Punjab provincial election the same day.
Ghurki was contesting a by-election called after the killing three months ago of Shaukat Butt, who had fought the February 3 polls as an independent and then joined the PML.
His constituency, in the Bagh Banpura district adjacent to the Pakistani-Indian border, has a reputation for violence involving rival gangs of smugglers and racketeers.
